plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you pay the second-highest bid only if you win, and any deviation from truthful bidding either causes you to lose profitable wins or win unprofitable ones. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26, ensuring optimal expected profit given the game's mechanics.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a private value of $18, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $18, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay less than my value when I do win.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a price exceeding my value (loss), while bidding lower risks losing an auction I could have profitably won. With my value at $21, the optimal action is to bid exactly $21, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair second-highest price.
